newsitem.title: USA: Aiken County, S.C., cities seek sales tax vote.
newsitem.headline: Aiken County, S.C., cities seek sales tax vote.

text.p: City councils in Aiken and North Agusta, S.C., have urged Aiken County to revive a local option sales tax proposal that was rejected by voters in 1992, the Agusta Chronicle said.
Both cities passed resolutions this month asking the county to place the original version of the tax proposal back on the ballot in November.
County officials told the newspaper there may not be time for a November referendum because of the public readings and reviews required.

The original version rejected by voters in 1992 would allow the county to raise the sales tax by one cent, to six percent. New revenues would be used mainly to roll back property taxes, with the state receiving a small portion and the remainder divided among the county and its municipalities.

Two other options since approved by the state legislature would allow the same tax increase to fund transportation projects, or to finance capital projects selected by an independent commission appointed by the county and its municipalities.
